The rapid advancement of smart mining technologies has significantly increased the demand for intelligent systems capable of ensuring continuous safety monitoring and timely hazard prediction in underground mining environments. Traditional safety monitoring methods are mostly dependent on manual monitoring, single sensor monitoring, or some rules-based methods, with the disadvantages of late monitoring of hazards, limited situational awareness, and low prediction precision when the scene changes in the mining operations. To overcome these limitations, the paper proposes DLOSM-EHWS (Deep Learning-Driven Online Safety Monitoring and Early Hazard Warning System for Smart Mines), an intelligent framework that integrates deep learning with real-time monitoring to identify hazardous conditions and provide early warning alerts for improving mine safety. The proposed framework uses visual and sensor information to continuously monitor the working environment, miners and equipment, allowing abnormal events, as well as potential hazardous situations, to be detected at an early stage. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DLOSM-EHWS framework, achieving an accuracy of 98.76%, precision of 98.42%, recall of 98.15%, F1-score of 98.28%, and a false alarm rate of 1.42%. The findings demonstrate reliable hazard detection, accurate prediction of the safety-risk, and efficient real-time online safety monitoring in the smart mining environment. The proposed DLOSM-EHWS framework enhances proactive risk management, supports intelligent decision-making, and contributes to safer, more resilient, and sustainable smart mining operations. Not applicable.

This project focuses on the mechanical design and development of an automated motorized stair lift to assist elderly and mobility-impaired individuals across multi-level buildings. The primaryobjective is to create a safe, cost-effective, and user-friendly mobility solution that operateson straight or curved staircases without requiring invasive architectural modifications. The mechanical architecture utilizes a robust aluminum or steel track securely mounted to the stair treads, supporting a load-bearing carriage assembly. Propulsion is achieved through a high-torque direct-current (DC) electric motor coupled with a rack-and-pinion drive system for smooth, controlled vertical transit. Continuous and reliable power is ensured via onboard rechargeable batteries, which also provide uninterrupted operation during primary power grid failures. The control system incorporates ergonomic armrest switches and wireless remote pendants located at the terminal landings for convenient call-and-send functionality. Advanced safety features include sensitive mechanical obstacle-detection edges on the footrest and carriage to instantly halt motion upon encountering blockages. Emergency redundancy is maintained through automatic over-speed governors, mechanical spring-applied brakes, and physical limit switches to prevent terminal over-travel. Ergonomic considerations feature a swiveling seat, foldable armrests, and a retractable footrest to maximize clearance and ease of transfer for the user. Ultimately, the developed prototype bridges a crucial accessibility gap, demonstrating high structural reliability, fail-safe redundancy, and enhanced independent living.
topics: Assistive Technology in Communication and Mobility

documents.abstract: Traffic signal control (TSC) is critical for mitigating urban congestion. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has achieved strong performance by learning adaptive policies from traffic observations, but learned neural controllers are often opaque, structurally complex, and difficult to generalize across scenarios. We propose PPL-TSC, a programmatic policy learning framework that distills compact and human-readable TSC policies from DRL teachers. PPL-TSC formulates policy learning as an evolutionary search over phase utility functions (PUFs), which score candidate signal phases and select the highest-utility phase for execution. Each generation consists of four steps: policy generation, policy review, policy calibration, and policy evaluation. In the generation step, a large language model (LLM) acts as a semantics-aware evolutionary operator to propose and refine candidate PUFs. Generated PUFs are screened through explicit checks for syntactic validity, mathematical soundness, and consistency with TSC principles, with invalid ones repaired through iterative feedback. Valid PUFs are then calibrated to improve behavioral fidelity to the DRL teacher, and evaluated using a joint score combining teacher fidelity and traffic-control performance to select candidates for the next generation. Extensive experiments across diverse traffic scenarios and representative DRL-based controllers show that PPL-TSC produces compact and human-readable policies, achieves competitive performance for most teacher families, improves transfer generalization, and substantially reduces computational cost. Code is available at https://github.com/ForrestXie9/PPL-TSC.

Benchmark of whether large language models match diagnostic specificity to the evidence in a case. 232 text vignettes of autonomic disorders (orthostatic hypotension subtypes, carotid sinus syndrome, vasovagal syncope subtypes), built from a specialist-reviewed diagnostic rulebook and drafted with large-language-model assistance. The set includes 70 paired twins in which the result that defines the subtype is removed and 14 twins in which the numbers are changed so the correct subtype flips. Five models are tested: gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3.8-27B, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and Gemma 4 31B through free APIs, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 through the Claude web chat in fresh, isolated conversations with memory, personalization and web search off. Primary endpoints: under-naming of supported subtypes, over-naming of subtypes on evidence-removed twins, and the paired difference, tested with one-sided exact McNemar tests (Holm-corrected across the five models). This registration was filed after answers from the four API models were collected (from 12 Nov 2026) but before any answer was scored or analysed; Claude answers are collected after registration. Cases, prompts and scorer were frozen on 11 Nov 2026 (SHA-256 fingerprints in the attached file). No human participants or patient data.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Typed Decision Models such as TypeSafe's Jev, also called System One or System 1 models, answer typed questions about an input with a probability for each option, and they need no training. Many NLP papers still fine-tune a task-specific classifier, and prompted large language models (LLMs) trail such classifiers on most text classification benchmarks. We ask how many of these fine-tuned classifiers a Typed Decision Model can replace under each paper's own evaluation, and what is needed where it cannot. We swap the predictors of 24 ACL-venue papers for Jev, keep each paper's splits, label definitions and metric, and check the results with Cloudflare's Clef, Microsoft-Decision-1 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna Decisions. The resulting 46 English test sets, with their questions and published scores, form the TDM-Gauntlet benchmark. With a zero-shot prompt, Jev directly replaced the paper's predictor on 12 of the 46 test sets, mostly single judgments with plain labels, but rarely where the paper's method was trained on its labels. Where Jev scored lower, we most often attributed the shortfall to an annotation convention that the label name does not state. With 500 training labels plus validation and no user-managed GPU, calibration and GEPA-style prompt optimization closed a median 72% of the gap to the paper's method, about twice what off-the-shelf GEPA closed, for a median $1.66 per search. On the same labels, fine-tuned encoders such as RoBERTa and DeBERTa closed 59%, and LoRA fine-tuning of the open LLM Qwen3.8-27B closed 97%. Fine-tuning remains the most accurate option, but a zero-shot prompt is often enough for plain labels, and prompt optimization closes most of the remaining gap.

Purpose: This study investigated the factors that predict senior high school students' interest in and attitudes toward Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education in Ghana. It examined how intrinsic motivation, self-determination, self-efficacy, career motivation, and grade motivation were linked to students' emotional engagement in STEM learning. Design/Methodology/Approach: This quantitative cross-sectional study used a structured questionnaire measured on a five-point Likert scale to collect data from 767 students. Students in Forms 1 to 3 were selected through proportional stratified sampling at three purposively selected senior high schools in the Greater Accra Region. Multiple regression analysis was used to identify the motivational factors that predict students’ interest in and attitude toward STEM. Research Limitation: This study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which restricts the ability to draw causal inferences. It also relied on self-reported data from students in one region of Ghana, which might limit its generalisability. Findings: The analysis showed that intrinsic motivation and self-determination strongly predict both STEM interest and attitudes. Self-efficacy and career motivation also predicted STEM interest but did not significantly predict attitude. In contrast, grade motivation predicts attitudes but not interest. The findings indicate that intrinsic motivation and self-determination are consistently associated with both STEM interest and STEM attitude, while other motivational factors show outcome-specific patterns. Practical Implication: The results suggest the need for educational changes that support student autonomy, promote inquiry-based learning, and improve career counselling. These changes can help connect teaching methods with motivational factors that maintain students’ interest and positive attitudes toward STEM. Social Implication: By highlighting the key psychological factors that drive STEM engagement, this study provides insights for policymakers looking to improve low STEM participation rates and encourage long-term economic development through more scientifically informed and skilled youth. Originality/Value: The findings indicate that STEM interest and attitudes reflect distinct motivational patterns. Intrinsic motivation and self-determination predict students’ STEM interest and STEM attitude, while self-efficacy and career motivation predict interest, and grade motivation predicts attitudes. It extends context-specific evidence and supports differentiated interpretations of STEM motivation.

This registration documents the analysis plan for a 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment examining how the actual source (credentialed counseling professional vs. generative AI) and the presented source label (human counselor vs. AI) of empathic-validating responses produced under identical content specifications influence perceived validation, and whether the label effect is associated with experience mind perception as a hypothesized indirect path, distinct from agency. Participants (Korean adults, ages 20–59) read three friendship-transgression scenarios, each followed by one response produced under identical content specifications and blind fidelity screening. Hypotheses and exclusion criteria were documented in the IRB-approved protocol (Sookmyung Women’s University IRB, SMWU-2609-HR-147) prior to data collection; this analysis plan is registered while collection is ongoing (392 responses collected toward a target of 400) and prior to any inferential analysis, with interim descriptive monitoring disclosed in the registration.

Reflective skill optimizers improve multi-turn LLM agents by revising instructions from failed and successful rollouts, yet accumulating edge-case rules bloats prompts, inflates token use, and pushes agents into long, error-prone loops. We introduce EfficientSkill, a two-step framework that first discovers a reliable skill without token penalties, and then warm-starts accuracy-guarded pruning from that skill to compress instructions, bound agent turns, and offload reusable code into workspace utilities with zero implementation prompt cost. Across four frontier, mid-tier, and open-weight models on MATH-500, ALFWorld, and SpreadsheetBench, EfficientSkill cuts output tokens over unconstrained EvoSkill on 11 of 12 configurations (by up to 80%) while raising mean accuracy on every benchmark, including +14.3 and +17.5 percentage-point gains on SpreadsheetBench with Gemini 3.8 Flash and Grok 4.1 Fast by replacing stalled loops with compact workflows. By shrinking both generated tokens and replayed history, EfficientSkill lowers total token usage and serving cost across every evaluated configuration, with or without full-prefix KV caching.

Wellness programs for employees are becoming essential in manufacturing since occupational health, work organization, physical demands, and psychosocial conditions can affect worker wellness and functional performance. This paper reviews the impact of programmes which enhance health in the workplace on productivity and job satisfaction in a manufacturing setting. A systematic critical assessment was conducted of peer-reviewed intervention studies, systematic reviews and authoritative occupational-health advice related specifically to Covid-19 pandemic and literature from 2020-2026 including relevant earlier studies. The existing body of research deals with both the promotion of physical health and risk management and stress management approaches. Programs that improve health behaviours, perceived wellbeing, work ability and other aspects of employee experience can be effective, according to the research. Nonetheless, the proof pertaining to absenteeism, objectively assessed output, and job satisfaction consistently shows improvement. The differences in study design, participant selection, duration of programme, measurement of outcome and context of industry prohibits direct comparisons and causality interpretation. The findings revealed that integrating individual support with risk mitigation can enhance the efficacy of wellness programs for manufacturing employees. In addition, supportive supervision, employee involvement, and execution consistent with shift schedules and production requirements are also favorable. The research also reveals that self-reported productivity as a proxy for verified production cannot address limitation and there are not enough rigorous longitudinal studies in manufacturing. Future studies should combine established job-satisfaction measurement instruments with objectively recorded measurement of output, quality, absence, and safety indicators, while also exploring programme costs, equity of access, and longer-term sustainability.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Ergonomically unfavorable postures remain a major risk factor for work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WRMSDs) among ultrasound operators. Dermatologic and facial ultrasound presents specific ergonomic challenges because it requires delicate transducer manipulation and prolonged static postures. This narrative review examines key ergonomic strategies for dermatologic and facial ultrasound, integrating findings from recent kinematic and occupational studies to promote sustainable, high-quality ultrasound practice. Important considerations include probe handling, scanning technique, patient positioning, and operator posture. Technical innovations, including portable systems, footswitches, and hands-free controls, are discussed, together with education, awareness, training, and future directions. A practical ergonomic workflow for facial ultrasound is also presented. Standardization of patient positioning, ultrasound-system layout, and operator ergonomics is essential for achieving reproducible diagnostic quality while safeguarding practitioner health. Although direct prospective clinical trials specifically addressing facial ultrasound ergonomics remain limited, translating evidence from general ultrasound and interventional practices provides a practical framework for clinical optimization.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

The overarching goal of reinforcement learning (RL) is to efficiently optimize the agent's policy for various environments, tasks, dynamics, and even user preferences, which often consist of multiple and potentially conflicting rewards/objectives. This necessitates the learning of Pareto-optimal policies that can navigate different trade-offs among objectives. However, existing multi-objective RL (MORL) methods, whether trained online or offline, are typically limited to task- or objective-specific policy learning and do not address generalization of learned trade-offs to unseen tasks/objectives. In this work, we propose the Foundation Pareto Flow Policy (FP2) for offline MORL in continuous robotic control, inspired by the pre-mid-post-training paradigm underlying recent foundation models. Specifically, we instantiate FP2 as a multi-modal diffusion transformer equipped with a likelihood-free flow matching loss, enabling unified, scalable, and instructable learning of diverse trade-off trajectories. We further develop a three-stage training pipeline to gradually optimize the policy: (1) pre-training on a large-scale MORL dataset, (2) mid-training on a carefully curated high-quality dataset, and (3) post-training on few collected trajectory data from new tasks and trade-offs. Empirical results demonstrate that FP2 outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods on most tasks of the D4MORL benchmark, achieving superior zero-shot interpolation and extrapolation on complex Pareto manifolds as well as efficient few-shot adaptation of the learned trade-off prior to new continuous-control tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/FibonacciRabbit/FP2.

Pictograms are a core modality in augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), yet recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) cannot reliably interpret or produce pictogram sequences. Two obstacles explain this gap: the absence of a standardized pictogram grammar and the scarcity of parallel text-pictogram data. We introduce Retrieval-Augmented Pictogram Selection (RAPS), an annotation method that refines a rule-based transcription system's output with LLM-based concept extraction and retrieval over a pictogram vocabulary, handling cases where hand-written rules fail (named entities, numbers, polysemous words) without requiring new rules. Applied to French, RAPS yields a synthetic corpus of 1.4 million parallel pairs, of which 300k are publicly released. In a human ranking study where annotators order four pictogram transcriptions of the same sentence, RAPS outperforms the rule-based state of the art. Moreover, we show that standard reference-based metrics separate systems of clearly different quality but fail to rank strong systems against each other. Finally, we build an instruction-tuned model that supports interaction in several AAC modalities: it accepts pictogram or text input and answers in pictograms, speech, or text.
topics: Assistive Technology in Communication and Mobility

documents.abstract: Vision-language models can turn road images into clear, geometry-aware pothole warnings, but current systems depend on commercial cloud services. Our earlier five-stage pipeline needed two cloud calls per scene, taking about 20 s and USD 0.105, and could not run offline. We rebuild every stage to run on a single local GPU and evaluate it with the same data, prompts, and protocol. Segmentation keeps the original Segment Anything weights but runs them in half precision with graph compilation, which makes it 2.7x faster without changing any downstream risk class; five lightweight variants could not match its masks on small road defects. Severity is graded by six ConvNeXt students distilled from 3092 cloud labels. They reach Cohen's kappa = 0.268 against human consensus at 28 ms per pothole, close to the cloud model's 0.321, within the camera setup they were trained for. A local 8-billion-parameter vision-language model writes the warnings under a grammar that admits only in-lane maneuvers. Three blind, independent raters scored these warnings safer than the cloud warnings (4.18 vs. 3.65 of 5; p = 0.001; 50 scenes) and equally clear, whereas an automated LLM judge ranked them the other way. The complete pipeline runs at 1.27 s per scene, 16x faster than the cloud system, offline and at no per-scene cost.
topics: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

documents.abstract: Generative AI can support learning, but it may also encourage cognitive outsourcing by replacing learners’ own thinking. This study reframes AI from an information provider to a responsive listener that promotes cognitive engagement and self-explanation. We introduce Hearble, a minimal robotic listener designed to isolate the effects of different backchannel modalities. Using a between-subjects design, we compare four conditions: no response, visual, nonverbal acoustic, and verbal backchannels. We examine how these conditions affect utterance elaboration, cognitive load, immediate comprehension, knowledge transfer, and perceived agency. Rather than limiting AI intervention to preserving learners’ cognitive processes, we investigate whether AI can actively support them by encouraging learners to articulate and elaborate their own thoughts. This work presents the physical AI listener as an alternative interaction paradigm for learning and provides a controlled foundation for future research on how embodiment, facial expressions, gestures, and other audience cues shape learning and agency.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

When a storm surge approaches a coastal town, the emergency plan must be put into action quickly using water-level forecasts, flood extent, road access, vulnerable residents and shelters. Bringing this information together under time pressure is slow and depends on the duty officer's expertise. This paper is one step in a wider research line from data to safe decisions: machine learning to understand the hazard, reinforcement learning and planning to choose actions, large language models (LLMs) to explain and cross-check them, and an assurance layer that keeps people in charge. Here we address the action step on a real place. We ask whether a policy can learn the timing of emergency actions from decades of real events. Lido di Venezia is represented as a heterogeneous graph built from public elevation, road, building and census data and driven by hourly tide-gauge records from 1983 to 2024, with seven actions taken from the municipal emergency plan. A PPO policy is trained on this graph and compared, on storm windows unseen in training, with a rule-based system simulating the officer's discretionary decisions. On 18 historical test scenarios, PPO achieves a similar reduction in population exposure to the rule. With uncertain forecasts and limited protection it again performs similarly but does not outperform the tuned rule, and removing graph message passing does not substantially reduce performance. PPO therefore learns an effective protective response from an outcome-based reward alone: it is given the plan's actions and when each is allowed, but not the thresholds that tell the comparator when to act. Next steps test harder edge cases, move closer to a digital twin of the territory, and replace the simulated officer with assessment by emergency-management stakeholders, supported by LLM-based interpretation of each recommendation.

Chinese outputs of large language models carry a perceptible "AI flavor": formulaic sentence frames, stacked written-register connectives, repetition loops, and layout leakage. A popular hypothesis blames text-only training for the missing inner-speech layer of human writing; injecting speech or prosody signals should therefore reduce it. We test it with controlled interventions on a 0.6B model; all three fail: (i) phoneme-interleaved continued pretraining yields no spokenness gain under text-matched controls while raising repetition (+0.13 [+0.03, +0.23]); (ii) prosody-plan conditional generation reaches an adherence of only 0.257 against a pre-registered 0.50 gate; (iii) a rule-based reward built on TTS prosody-feature distance is imperceptible in double-blind evaluation by both humans (8/16) and a calibrated LLM judge (9/16). A root cause is evaluation: single-rater blind evaluation at n~20 only detects extreme (>=85%) preferences. We therefore build a calibrated LLM-judge protocol: the judge passes catch trials on known-answer pairs (16/16; single-text 22/24, same-topic pairs 24/24, versus 0.75 for the human rater), then annotates with two independent judges under A/B swapping, counting disagreement as a tie. Using the judge's agree labels directly as DPO pairs (no reward model), we obtain the first positive result: held-out blind win rate 0.833 [0.699, 0.972], repetition 0.114 to 0.000, unchanged MMLU. We further identify a Goodhart channel: the judge's length preference transduces into output-length collapse via pairwise DPO (median 75 chars vs a 300-char prompt); an SFT-anchor repairs it (w is a style knob: w=0.1 preserves gains, w=0.3 does not). Scaling preference data from 89 to 240 pairs yields no additional judge-visible gain. We release RA-Eval v0.1: a three-layer Chinese AI-flavor evaluation framework with 382 judge-annotated preference pairs.

Memory systems allow AI agents to persist information across interactions, making them more personalized and more capable on long-horizon tasks. This persistence introduces new risks: stored information can be disclosed in inappropriate contexts, resist correction or deletion, be retained beyond what users desire, or be poisoned to influence later agent behaviour. Yet memory systems are typically evaluated on task performance and efficiency alone. We argue that a memory system should instead be understood as the custodian of its user's persistent information, with responsibilities that extend beyond helping an agent complete its tasks, and that it should be evaluated holistically against all such responsibilities. We present Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems (HEAMS), an open-source framework for evaluating agent memory systems in this way. First, we state the responsibilities of agent memory systems as explicit behavioural desiderata spanning performance, efficiency, security, privacy, and user sovereignty. Second, we assemble a benchmark suite that covers these desiderata and acknowledge the gaps that remain. Third, we develop MilaMem, a prototype memory system, and a governance layer that can wrap any memory system, enabling controlled study of memory system design choices. Fourth, we compare memory systems across the full HEAMS benchmark suite. We find that no memory system leads every performance benchmark, and strong performance scores may coexist with poor privacy, user-sovereignty, and security scores. Governance strongly influences results: recall policies can reduce inappropriate disclosure at a cost in helpfulness, while both recall and retention policies improve poisoning resistance. Performance and efficiency benchmarks alone therefore cannot reveal how well a memory system meets its responsibilities. Code: https://github.com/milatechtransfer/heams
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: When LLMs turn requirements into code, every underspecified constraint becomes behavior that the model must decide during generation. We test when specifications move beyond structure and begin to control generated behavior. In a controlled experiment, 72 participants implemented and revised Python tasks with an LLM under three levels of specification explicitness. The results show a clear break between lightweight structure and explicit behavioral obligations. Lightweight structure reduced hidden-test failures by only 8.7%. Requiring participants to specify constraints, invariants, negative requirements, edge cases, tie-breaking rules, and exception handling cut failures by 47.2% and reduced the number of distinct failure modes by 20.5%. The largest drops were in failure modes tied to implicit obligations. Invariant violations fell by 66.1%, and unsupported assumptions fell by 59.5%. After a requirement change, specifications with explicit behavioral obligations produced regressions in more submissions, but each affected submission lost less previously correct behavior. Explicit specifications also changed how developers judged generated code. Without explicit obligations, participants overestimated generated-code correctness by about 23 percentage points. With explicit obligations, they produced better code but judged it more cautiously. Thus, the lesson is sharper than "better specifications help." Lightweight structure barely helped, while explicit behavioral obligations nearly halved failures, made regressions shallower, and improved calibration.

Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN functionals. Additionally, IANN provides an agent interface to facilitate integration with autonomous agents.

Objective: This study describes how an Akidah Akhlak teacher applies a humanistic approach at State Islamic Senior High School (Madrasah Aliyah Negeri, MAN) 2 Klaten, Indonesia, and interprets how these practices may support the conditions for students’ love of science. Theoretical framework: The analysis draws on Maslow’s hierarchy of needs, Rogers’ person-centred learning, Freire’s dialogical education and Deci and Ryan’s self-determination theory, and treats hubb al-ʿilm as an Islamic educational orientation that overlaps with, but is not identical to, intrinsic motivation. Literature review: The literature review examines humanistic Islamic education through Maslow, Rogers, Freire, and self-determination theory, highlighting the relationship between student autonomy, emotional needs, moral learning, and hubb al-ʿilm. Research gap: Earlier studies of humanistic Akidah Akhlak learning have mostly examined primary-level madrasahs and moral outcomes such as courtesy and discipline, leaving field evidence on knowledge-oriented outcomes at the Madrasah Aliyah level limited. Methods: A qualitative case study used semi-structured interviews, passive participatory classroom observation and documentation review. Data were analyzed with the interactive model of Miles, Huberman and Saldaña, and credibility was supported by source triangulation and member checking. Results: Three interrelated strategies emerged: differentiating methods according to class conduciveness; negotiating relational agreements that recognize students’ basic needs and autonomy, namely a responsibility-based eating and drinking policy and the absence of homework; and responding to mistakes with mild consequences followed by reflective dialogue on the purpose of seeking knowledge. Together, these practices appear to create a low-threat climate that is conducive to curiosity and to a shift from external towards more internalized motivation. Because the evidence rests mainly on the teacher’s account, supported by classroom observation and documents, the study does not claim that students’ love of science was measured or has increased. Implications: The three-stage model offered here is a contextual interpretation of one case, and may inform teacher reflection and training in comparable madrasahs. Novelty: The study foregrounds hubb al-ʿilm as an affective orientation in humanistic Akidah Akhlak learning at the Madrasah Aliyah level and documents concrete relational agreements that are rarely reported.

Industrial emergencies in refineries, petroleum terminals, chemical plants, and other high-hazard facilities require more than effective firefighting, process isolation, and rescue operations. They also demand timely, accurate, coordinated and stakeholder-specific communication. When information is delayed, inconsistent or inaccessible, operational response may be impeded, families may experience avoidable distress, emergency access may be obstructed, and confidence in the organization may be weakened. This paper examines three practitioner-observed industrial fire emergencies: a refinery fire/explosion in 1988, a fire at Jawahar Dweep in 2017, and a fire emergency encountered during an occupational health, safety, and environment audit. The cases are used as retrospective practitioner illustrations rather than as a statistically representative or conventionally documented qualitative dataset. The paper distinguishes direct observations and recollections from interpretations informed by emergency-communication literature and from the managerial framework proposed by the author. It develops an Industrial Crisis Communication Framework covering preparedness, detection and notification, command and information verification, stakeholder-specific dissemination, monitoring and feedback, and post-emergency learning. Attention is given to family information arrangements, communication redundancy, the separation of operational command channels from public-facing communication, vulnerable stakeholders, misinformation, cyber resilience, and measurable readiness. A preliminary readiness scorecard is proposed for pilot testing in tabletop and full-scale exercises. The framework is intended as a practical, auditable aid for plant-specific emergency preparedness; its effectiveness requires prospective validation.

Multicultural education in Hong Kong poses learning challenges. For example, non-Chinese-speaking (NCS) students and newly-arrived students (NAS) come from diverse linguistic backgrounds. However, existing interventions emphasise unidirectional instruction. This study addresses the gap by investigating how an interactive robot-assisted scenario (RAS) system can support Cantonese instruction in multicultural classrooms. We employ a mixed-method approach examining quantitative engagement measures and qualitative experiential data. We investigate how RAS intervention can influence the engagement and motivation of NAS and NCS students to learn Cantonese, and the impacts of RAS on the Cantonese proficiency outcomes of NAS and NCS learners. Findings reveal differential engagement patterns: NAS demonstrate improvements in behavioural engagement, while NCS students show a slight decline in cognitive engagement. This research contributes to human-agent interaction (HAI) by examining cross-cultural learning dynamics and providing preliminary insights for the development of multicultural educational technologies.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Reinforcement learning via environmental interaction is a cornerstone post-training paradigm for evolving large language models into autonomous agents capable of multi-turn tool use and exploration. Because the environment defines what the policy observes and how actions are verified, its structure directly bounds the capabilities an agent can acquire. Yet existing structured and retrieval environments rely on upstream pre-filtering---extracting a compact subgraph around the gold answer or retrieving fixed passages before the policy acts. We show that such pre-filtering introduces a fundamental measurement confound: because per-question subgraphs enclose ground-truth paths, they compress the candidate space by orders of magnitude and leak answer locations via local topology, allowing a question-blind degree heuristic to surface gold answers far above chance. To restore path selection, candidate pruning, and optimal stopping as genuine policy decisions, we propose RISE (Interactive Structured Environment), which transitions structured reinforcement learning from static subgraphs to full-scale interactive databases along two coupled axes. First, Decision-Space Scaling exposes the unpruned knowledge graph via a five-stage graph-agnostic typed intent adapter under a bounded call budget and a multiplicative grounding reward gate. Second, Learning-Frontier Scaling overcomes within-group variance collapse under group-normalized objectives by uniting model-independent structural tier progression with a self-evolving competence-frontier bandit. Across nineteen benchmarks and three model backbones, RISE substantially advances in-domain and unseen-schema knowledge-graph reasoning, transfers zero-shot to open-domain passage retrieval, and significantly enhances out-of-domain mathematical and logical deduction.

This systematic review examines interventions designed to regulate cognitive offloading to generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and their effects on subsequent independent performance in educational and employee development contexts. The review aims to identify how interventions structure the distribution of cognitive work between individuals and GenAI, evaluate their effects on learning and task performance after AI assistance has been withdrawn, and examine the conditions under which these effects may differ. Eligible evidence will include comparative experimental and quasi-experimental studies assessing independent knowledge, skills or task performance following GenAI-supported activities. Electronic searches were conducted in six bibliographic databases and preprint repositories, followed by deduplication and pilot screening. Two reviewers will independently screen studies and extract data. The review will use structured descriptive synthesis, supplemented by meta-analysis where the evidence permits. Risk of bias will be assessed using JBI tools, and certainty of evidence for key outcomes will be evaluated using GRADE. The expected contribution is an evidence-based understanding of which approaches to regulating cognitive offloading have been evaluated, what effects they produce on independent performance, and how confidently these effects can be interpreted. Findings may inform the design of GenAI-supported education and employee development activities.

We present a library of formally verified graph algorithms in Isabelle/HOL. The library covers the main problems of combinatorial optimisation on graphs: reachability, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, matching, maximum flow, and minimum-cost flow. The algorithms in the library use most of the standard algorithm design techniques: graph search, greedy algorithms on matroids, dynamic programming, augmenting paths, blossom contraction, blocking flows, push-relabel, scaling, the primal-dual method, randomisation, and certificate checking. The library has adaptors between different types of graphs (directed, undirected, multigraphs), which allow results to be reused. Each algorithm is verified independently of its data structures, and the main algorithms are refined to efficient imperative implementations, from which we generate code in Standard ML, Scala, and Go. We developed parts of the library with large language models (LLMs), improved the quality of their proofs with a method based on statistics of our own proofs, and labelled which parts were developed by humans, by LLMs, or collaboratively. We perform a detailed experimental analysis of representative algorithms in our library, comparing it with state-of-the-art mainstream libraries, showing that our implementations are practical.

Overview & Rationale for Structural Redesign The Philippines relies on foreign manufacturers for 99.9% of its medical equipment. While domestic engineering and clinical talent are abundant, academic and local research initiatives frequently stall before reaching clinical deployment due to fragmented workflows, unharmonized regulatory standards, and complex, intimidating Quality Management System (QMS) documentation. Without a clear lifecycle structure, up to 70% of medical equipment in resource-constrained settings fails prematurely due to unaddressed design barriers, missing consumables, or inadequate maintenance pathways. This derivative working manual restructures the comprehensive 21-section ISOXIAN Framework (ISOX-MDR-2026-001) into an actionable, persona-based operational guide designed to shift academic teams from grant-driven prototyping to commercial, regulatory-compliant manufacturing (ISO 13485, ISO 14971, IEC 62366, and PH FDA AO 2020-0010). To maximize comprehension and eliminate cognitive overload for first-time adopters, this edition introduces four structural innovations: Pre-Project Gate 0 (UX Research & Market Validation): Mandates user persona mapping, clinical journey analysis, and target market interviews before engineering resources or procurement are approved, preventing academic teams from building solutions without clinical or commercial viability. Role-Isolated Chapters: Replaces dense cross-functional matrices with dedicated chapters for each project role (Top Management, QMO, PRRC, Product Manager, Project Leader, Hardware/Software Engineers, Clinical/Usability Evaluators, and Asset/IT Administrators). The Toyota Way (Lean Operational Execution): Embeds Genchi Genbutsu (go and see), Jidoka (built-in quality and immediate error stopping), Heijunka (leveled Kanban workflows), and continuous improvement (Kaizen) directly into daily engineering and regulatory tasks. Prolonged computer use may increase ergonomic risk among educational support staff when workplace facilities are not suitable. This study aimed to describe the level of ergonomic risk among 41 educational support staff at Universitas Esa Unggul, Jakarta, using the Rapid Office Strain Assessment (ROSA) method. The study used a cross-sectional design with a descriptive quantitative approach and stratified random sampling. Data were collected through direct observation and ROSA assessment of chair, monitor, telephone, keyboard, and mouse components, then analyzed using frequency distributions and percentages. The results showed that 87.8% of educational support staff were categorized as having high ergonomic risk, while 12.2% were in the moderate-risk category. The highest ROSA score was 7, found in 56.1% of respondents. Problems with the chair component were most frequently found in the armrests and backrests, and all chairs lacked adjustable features for the seat and backrest. These findings indicate the need to improve workplace facilities, particularly chair suitability and adjustability, as part of ergonomic risk control among educational support staff.

We present Lao Siji, an end-to-end driving policy that ranks third in the 2026 NVIDIA AlpaSim E2E Driving Challenge, ahead of most entries built on foundation models. Instead of training from scratch on a general-purpose vision backbone, we adapt openpilot, an open-source L2 production model. We freeze its vision encoder and fine-tune the policy layers with an ego-state adapter and a route memory. On closed-loop rollouts in neural-reconstructed scenes, we supervise the policy with a privileged map teacher for lateral self-correction and a body-extent loss for road and obstacle clearance, while distilling the base model's remaining outputs to retain car following. Ablations show that self-correction samples carry the gain, while the clearance loss substitutes for them where no teacher exists. Longitudinal safety instead rests on the base model's lead-vehicle estimate behind a rule-based speed layer. Longer training, imitating human logs, and human-log speed targets yield either no measurable gain or adverse effects. Without further training, Lao Siji also places among the leaders on HUGSIM and Odyssey. The final training takes only one GPU-hour and shifts the weights by 3.9% from the shipped model. Code will be released after review.

The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface configuration. We introduce a functional taxonomy of LLM-enabled wireless resource management strategies and analyze the prompt engineering methodologies employed in recent literature. Furthermore, we develop a generalized analytical framework that categorizes LLM-based optimization architectures, including direct solution generation, closed-loop optimization with external verifiers, and representation encoding within trainable neural pipelines. To demonstrate practical applicability, we present representative case studies on LLM-assisted beam prediction for millimeter-wave systems and adaptive wireless resource allocation. Finally, we discuss emerging hybrid AI approaches for wireless networks.

There is growing interest in understanding how people interact with large language models (LLMs) and whether such models elicit dependency or even addictive behaviour. Validated tools to assess the extent to which individuals may become dependent on LLMs are scarce and primarily build on classic behavioural addiction symptoms, adapted to the context of LLM use. We view this as a conceptual limitation, as the LLM-human relationship is more nuanced and warrants a fresh and distinct perspective. To address this gap, we developed and validated a new 12-item questionnaire to measure LLM dependency, referred to as LLM-D12. The scale was based on the authors’ prior theoretical work, with items developed accordingly and responses collected from 526 participants in the UK. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, performed on separate halves of the total sample using a split-sample approach, supported a two-factor structure: Instrumental Dependency (six items) and Relationship Dependency (six items). Instrumental Dependency reflects the extent to which individuals rely on LLMs to support or collaborate in decision-making and cognitive tasks. Relationship Dependency captures the tendency to perceive LLMs as socially meaningful, sentient, or companion-like entities. The two-factor structure demonstrated excellent internal consistency and clear discriminant validity. External validation confirmed both the conceptual foundation and the distinction between the two subscales. The psychometric properties and structure of our LLM-D12 scale were interpreted in light of the emerging view that dependency on LLMs does not necessarily indicate dysfunction but may still reflect reliance levels that could become problematic in certain contexts.

Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .

Balancing employment, graduate education, and personal responsibilities has become a growing challenge for working professionals pursuing advanced degrees in public administration. This phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of Master in Business Administration (MBA) students at Northeastern College, Santiago City, Philippines, in managing work-life-learning balance. Guided by Husserlian phenomenology, the study sought to understand how graduate students navigate competing professional, academic, and personal demands while sustaining academic performance and personal well-being. Purposive sampling was employed to select fifteen MBA students who were simultaneously employed in government agencies, local government units, educational institutions, and private organizations. Data were gathered through semi-structured, in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological method. Findings revealed five essential themes: (1) navigating competing professional and academic responsibilities; (2) strategic time management and prioritization; (3) institutional and family support as catalysts for persistence; (4) psychological resilience amid multiple role demands; and (5) graduate education as a pathway toward professional advancement and public service excellence. Participants described balancing multiple responsibilities as challenging yet transformative, enabling them to strengthen leadership competencies, decision-making abilities, organizational skills, and public service commitment. Despite experiencing fatigue, stress, and occasional work-life conflicts, students demonstrated resilience through effective planning, support systems, and intrinsic motivation to achieve career advancement. The study underscores the importance of flexible institutional policies, responsive graduate programs, and supportive workplace environments that foster academic persistence among working professionals. The findings contribute to the growing body of literature on adult learning, work-life balance, and graduate education within the context of Philippine public administration.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. To assess reasoning quality, an LLM-based judge evaluated correctly answered responses using a multidimensional rubric. Although responses generally demonstrated strong problem comprehension, they scored lower in factual and procedural accuracy and distractor analysis, indicating that correct answers were not necessarily supported by technically sound justifications. Response clarity was also weakly indicative of technical quality. Furthermore, longer reasoning traces were associated with lower accuracy in both frontier reasoning models, suggesting that reasoning length may reflect question difficulty rather than improved problem-solving performance. Reasoning-token consumption may therefore provide an additional signal for identifying potentially unreliable responses. NEBench R1 establishes a benchmark for evaluating both answer accuracy and reasoning quality, providing a foundation for assessing the domain competence and reliability of LLMs in nuclear engineering.

The growing integration of GenAI into luxury services raises important questions in a domain where exclusivity, authenticity, uniqueness, and human touch are central. Integrating sociotechnical theory with AI‐in‐service and luxury research, this study uses two experiments to examine how human‐only, GenAI‐only, and hybrid luxury service delivery configurations influence customer evaluations. Findings show that hybrid delivery produces the most favorable luxury service outcomes, with perceived authenticity explaining these effects and need for uniqueness (NFU) shaping customer responses across configurations. This research advances understanding of GenAI in luxury services by showing that its value depends on how human and technological capabilities are combined rather than on either mode in isolation. It also contributes to extant knowledge by showing that authenticity is not merely a stable attribute of luxury offerings, but a psychological mechanism affected by how the luxury service is delivered. Finally, it establishes NFU as a motivational boundary condition that explains variation in customer responses to different luxury service delivery configurations and its interplay with perceived authenticity. Practically, this research offers guidance on integrating GenAI in ways that preserve rather than undermine customer evaluations of luxury services.
topics: Consumer Behavior in Brand Consumption and Identification

documents.abstract: The manufacturing industry faces increasing pressure to improve productivity and production efficiency due to growing market demand and competition. Unbalanced workloads among workstations can result in excessive cycle times, bottlenecks, idle time, and line stoppages, which negatively affect production performance. These problems are particularly critical in mass-production systems, where consistent cycle time and balanced workload distribution are essential to maintaining stable production flow. This study focuses on a motorcycle manufacturing line producing automatic motorcycles, where several workstations were identified as having cycle times exceeding the established standard. This study aims to improve production line balance by reducing cycle time deviations, redistributing workloads, and increasing overall line efficiency. The study applies a line balancing approach using the Ranked Positional Weight (RPW) method and a heuristic method. Cycle time data were collected from individual workstations and analyzed to identify overloaded and underutilized stations. The improvement process involved redistributing work elements from overloaded workstations to stations with available capacity, supported by layout adjustments and ergonomic considerations. The target cycle time was set at 22 seconds per workstation. The results show that three workstations initially exceeded the 22 second cycle time standard, with cycle times of 24.77 seconds, 23.28 seconds, and 24.43 seconds. After workload redistribution and process improvements, the cycle times of these workstations were reduced to 21.99 seconds, 21.70 seconds, and 21.87 seconds, respectively. The number of workstations was reduced from 22 to 18. Consequently, line efficiency increased from 81,04 % to 95,06 %, while balance delay decreased from approximately 18.96% to 4,94%. These findings demonstrate that integrating RPW, heuristic workload redistribution, and ergonomic layout improvements can effectively enhance production line balance, reduce bottlenecks, and improve production efficiency. The proposed approach provides a practical framework for continuous line balancing in motorcycle manufacturing and other mass-production environments

Large language models are trained to have safety guardrails, but these can be compromised while fine-tuning for new capabilities, such as reasoning. One way to mitigate this degradation is to modify the fine-tuning objective to preserve safety behaviour, but doing so effectively and efficiently remains challenging. We revisit Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), which penalises parameter updates based on sensitivity estimates from the diagonal of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). While EWC provides some protection, the diagonal approximation ignores interactions between parameters. We address this limitation by exploiting recent findings that safety-relevant behaviour is located in a low-rank subspace within models. Our method, Subspace-Projected Elastic Weight Consolidation (SP-EWC), projects gradients onto this subspace to capture non-diagonal curvature efficiently. We investigate three different ways of identifying the safety subspace: through safety fine-tuning updates (LoRA), safety-related activations (ActSVD), and contrastive representations of safety and utility data (cPCA). We find that this choice substantially affects performance, with SP-EWC using cPCA comparing favourably against existing methods by better maintaining safety guardrails without introducing excessive over-refusal.
